title: The Building Code
logline: Ted's building is sold to a mysterious company called Legendary Holdings, and the new landlord turns out to be Barney, who rolls out the Building Code: suit up in the lobby, a VIP section on the roof and a ten percent nacho tax. Ted organizes a rent strike with a union of three, Marshall reads the new lease twice, Lily climbs the ranks to Deputy Landlord, and Robin gets stuck as the super because a Canadian cannot let anyone freeze.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2012, my building got a new landlord. He had a dress code for the lobby, a velvet rope on the roof and a tax on nachos. It took him a week to become a tyrant. Okay, an afternoon. It took me a lot longer to figure out why he bought the place.

guests.name: Dolores Fink
guests.role: The eighty-one-year-old tenant in 2B and a veteran of the rent strike of 1977. Talks like a sweet grandmother, plans like a getaway driver, calls everyone sweetie and always has bolt cutters somewhere in her cardigan

scenes.summary: A letter under the door: the building has been sold to Legendary Holdings, with new rules. Marshall reads the sign: suit up in the lobby, a VIP section on the roof, a ten percent nacho tax. Ted objects that the Building Code is not a building code. Barney walks in without knocking: he's the landlord. Why buy a building? 'Please.' He won't knock now that he owns the door. Rule four, no etymology after nine. The heat dies: the super quit rather than suit up. Robin fixes the 1931 boiler with a slapshot from Ted's decorative hockey stick, and Barney makes her the super; she can't refuse, because in Canada letting people freeze is the only real crime. Lily flatters her way onto the VIP list. Ted declares a rent strike, though his rent is on autopay. Rules five and six. Button: Robin is management now and can't be seen with them.

beats.line: It started on a Tuesday night, with a letter slipped under our door.
The building's been sold. Our new landlord is a company called Legendary Holdings.
Give me that. I'm a lawyer. I read things all the way to the bottom.
New building rules, effective immediately. Rule three. A nacho tax. Ten percent, payable in chips.
beats.title: THE BUILDING CODE
lines: 2. The roof now has a VIP section.
3. Nacho tax: ten percent, payable in chips.

beats.line: Ten percent, Lily. The tenth chip is the one with all the cheese. They know. They know!
And they call it the Building Code? That is not what a building code is!
Ted, they're taxing nachos. The name is not the crime.
Legendary. Suit up. A VIP section. Who do we know who would—
Don't say it. If you say it, it's real.
Good evening, tenants.
You bought our building?
I bought your building, the dry cleaner downstairs and the pigeon on the fire escape. His rent is going up.
Barney, why would you buy an apartment building?
Please.
And you can't just barge in here anymore. Landlords have to give notice.
Ted, I haven't knocked on that door in seven years. I'm not starting now that I own it.
Barney. As a lawyer. Where is your legal authority for a nacho tax?
I'm the landlord, Marshall. I am the authority. And I've seen you eat. Ten percent of you is a lot of chips.
What exactly is in the VIP section?
Three lawn chairs, a cooler and bottle service. The bottle is beer. The service is me.
And suit up in the lobby? Barney, our lobby is a mailbox and a fern.
And now it's a mailbox, a fern and a dress code.
Actually, the word lobby comes from the Latin lobia, a covered walkway where monks would—
Rule four. No etymology after nine p.m.
Is it me, or did it just get really cold in here?
The radiator stopped clanking. It never stops. It clanks all night like a haunted xylophone.
Yeah, the super quit this morning. He refused to suit up. He said overalls are a lifestyle.
Where's the boiler?
Basement. It's from nineteen thirty-one. It hates everyone.
Ted, I'm borrowing your hockey stick.
That stick is decorative! I bought it to impress a girl from Winnipeg!
It's clanking! Lily, the xylophone is back!
Same boiler my dad had. You hit the main valve with a slapshot. Low and hard.
Robin Scherbatsky. Congratulations. You're the new super.
No.
Then the building freezes.
I'm Canadian, Barney. Letting people freeze is the only real crime we have. Everything else is an apology.
One week.
Welcome to management. There's a lanyard.
Barney. Has anyone ever told you that owning property looks really good on you?
Go on.
You have landlord eyes. Kind, but they could raise my rent at any moment.
Lily Aldrin. You're on the list.
Lily!
What? He has a roof. A VIP roof.
No. As of tonight, this tenant is on strike. Not one dollar of rent until the Building Code comes down.
Ted, your rent is on autopay.
Then tomorrow morning I'll call the bank and cancel it. During business hours. Like a revolutionary.
Rule five. No strikes.
You can't make a rule against—
Rule six. No telling the landlord what he can't make a rule against.
I should go. I'm management now. I can't be seen with you people.

scenes.summary: A week of the Building Code in a montage: a tie for the trash, the nacho tax, Ted not on the list. Day eight: Ted pickets outside the velvet rope with a chant that is really a memo, joined by Dolores Fink from 2B, veteran of 1977, who once put a landlord in a dumpster, gently. Lily lounges in the VIP section: not a scab, a VIP. Marshall wants Lily back and the yellow chair reclines. Ted points out the rope blocks the only path to the stairwell: an egress violation. Barney: only the vibe is being violated. Robin the super arrives exhausted; Dolores is leaving her the apartment; the boiler calls (runner 2). Barney's Rule forty closes the roof to strikers, Rule forty-one bans reminiscing. Dolores will bring bolt cutters. Lily escorts the strikers out: Marshall is not on the list.

beats.line: Within a week, the Building Code had forty rules, and Uncle Barney enforced every one personally.
It's six a.m., Barney. I'm taking out the trash.
And the trash deserves a tie.
Nacho tax.
Take the one with the most cheese. And take my dignity while you're at it.
Barney, I've lived in this building for nine years.
Sorry, sir. You're not on the list.
By day eight, I had done what any self-respecting architect would do. I had started a movement.
What do we want? Reasonable building policies! When do we want them? After a fair review period!
Sweetie, that's not a chant. That's a memo.
Ted, your union is you and Mrs. Fink from 2B.
Dolores, sweetie. I was in the rent strike of nineteen seventy-seven. We put a landlord in a dumpster.
Gently. He was fine. He moved to Florida.
They all end up in Florida.
Barney, my drink has gone warm.
Right away, Miss Aldrin.
Lily! You're a scab!
I'm not a scab, Ted. I'm a VIP. It's a totally different lanyard.
Lilypad. Come home. The union needs you. I need you. The nachos need you.
Name?
Barney, it's me. Her husband.
Is that a first name or a last name?
Baby, the yellow chair reclines.
Ted. It reclines.
Marshall! Solidarity!
And for the record, that rope blocks the only path to the stairwell. That's an egress violation.
Ted, the only thing being violated up here is the vibe.
Barney. I've been up since four. 5C's toilet is haunted, and the dry cleaner wants to unionize.
Unionize? With Ted?
Against Ted. He corrected the spelling on their sign.
Robin! My radiator works for the first time since nineteen ninety-four. I'm leaving you my apartment.
Mrs. Fink, you are going to outlive me.
That's the plan, sweetie.
Super.
Boiler's out. Fourth time today. Excuse me while I go hit the only thing in this building I respect.
Tenants. Rule forty. Effective immediately, the roof is closed to strikers. The super padlocks the door tonight.
You can't ban me from this roof! Every important conversation of my life happened on this roof!
Rule forty-one. No reminiscing on the roof.
A padlock? Don't you worry, sweetie. I'll bring the bolt cutters.
Dolores, we don't need bolt cutters.
Nobody ever thinks they need bolt cutters.
Miss Aldrin, would you escort the strikers off my roof?
With pleasure, Mister Stinson.
Lily, I'm your husband!
And you're not on the list, baby.

scenes.summary: The summit at landlord headquarters. Lily is now Deputy Landlord, earned by laughing at Barney's jokes about Marshall. Ted claims forty united units; flashback to the first union meeting: Ted, Marshall, Dolores, a sign about nachos and bolt cutters for no reason. So, three. Barney counteroffers a free tie. Marshall read the forty-one page lease twice, once as a lawyer and once as a man: the landlord's birthday is a building holiday, twice a year, and Rule Fourteen says no tenant may ever move out. Barney gets oddly flustered. Robin quits as super: the boiler is the healthiest relationship she's ever had, so it has to end. Then Barney mentions it's dropping to thirty tonight. Ted declares they'll take the roof. Tag: Lily has the sale papers. Barney paid three times the asking price to beat a condo developer who'd have emptied the building by spring. Barney begs her not to tell Ted, who'd write him a letter with a wax seal. Lily extorts a parking space and naming rights: kindergarten rules.

beats.line: Two days later, the Tenants' Union demanded a summit at landlord headquarters.
Gentlemen. Welcome. Deputy Landlord, scotch for our guests.
Right away, Mister Stinson.
Deputy Landlord? Lily, when did that happen?
Tuesday. I laughed at all his jokes. Even the ones about you.
Barney, I'm here on behalf of the tenants. Forty units. One voice. This building has never been more united.
Really. How many people came to your first meeting?
It was a powerful turnout.
Welcome, everyone, to the first meeting of the Tenants' Union!
Sweetie, where is everyone?
5C couldn't make it. They love the suit rule. They've met more women in that lobby than in college.
I made us a sign.
beats.title: TENANTS, UNITE!

beats.line: And I brought bolt cutters.
For what?
Sweetie, you never know what for until you know what for.
So. Three.
Three very committed people.
Two and a half. I left early for nachos.
Our demands. Repeal the suit rule. Open the roof. Abolish the nacho tax.
Counteroffer. Everything stays, and you get a free tie.
Then, as counsel for the union, let's talk about your new lease. I read all forty-one pages. Twice.
Once as a lawyer. And once as a man.
Page nine. The landlord's birthday is a building holiday. It's in March. And also October.
I'm a complicated man, Marshall.
And Rule Fourteen. No tenant may ever move out. Ever.
Ever? Barney, that's not a lease. That's a hostage situation with a laundry room.
It's standard.
It is not standard! I checked! I called a guy!
Deputy, is it hot in here? Somebody call the super.
Barney. I quit.
You can't quit. Rule thirty. The super serves at the pleasure of the landlord.
Then I'll stop being pleasant.
Robin. When have you ever been pleasant?
I've hit that boiler twenty-two times this week. It breaks down, I hit it, and nobody talks about feelings.
Sweetie, that sounds kind of perfect for you.
It's the healthiest relationship I've ever had. That's why I have to end it.
Fine. Quit. Shame about the weather. It's supposed to drop to thirty tonight.
Damn it.
Fine. The Tenants' Union has no choice. Tomorrow night, we take back the roof.
The roof door is padlocked, Ted.
We have bolt cutters.
We have Dolores.
Barney. While I was deputy-ing your desk, I found the sale papers. You paid three times the asking price.
Three times? For our building? The water pressure is a rumor.
And the other bidder was a condo developer. Everyone would have been out by spring.
Barney Stinson. Did you buy a whole building to save Ted's apartment?
Please.
Say please one more time, and I'm calling Ted.
Fine! Yes! But if Ted finds out, he'll make it a thing. He'll cry. He'll write me a letter. With a wax seal, Lily.
Then my silence has a price. One. A parking space.
You don't have a car.
I'll stand in it.
Two. The VIP section is now the Lily Aldrin Sky Lounge.
Lily, that's extortion.
It's kindergarten, Robin. You find out who has a crush on who, and you own them until June.

scenes.summary: The next night the Tenants' Union holds the VIP section. Robin left the padlock open; Dolores cut it anyway, for morale. The yellow chair reclines; Marshall smuggled untaxed nachos up the fire escape. Barney arrives with Lily and Robin. Robin is a super, not a bouncer: same lanyard. Ted pays off the egress plant with the real building code: one call and the fire department shuts the VIP section down. Barney can't believe the building code beats the Building Code. Ted demands the truth. Tax write-off, the hot yoga sightlines, then Lily threatens to do his voice. The honest version: the condo developer, everyone out by spring, and this apartment is the only door in New York Barney never has to knock on, so he bought the door, and the building around it, for structural reasons. He had to be a tyrant for his image. Rule Fourteen: that one he meant. Ted will write him a letter: oh no. The rules come down, except the nacho tax. Lily mourns the Sky Lounge. The boiler dies and Robin sprints for it: that's her boiler. Barney: and she says he has commitment issues. Future Ted closes the nacho question.

beats.line: The next night, the Tenants' Union took the roof.
Told you we'd need the bolt cutters, sweetie.
Dolores, the padlock was open. Robin left it unlocked for us.
I cut it anyway. For morale.
Ted. It reclines. We were fighting for the right thing.
And these nachos are untaxed. Smuggled them up the fire escape. They taste like freedom. And a little like fire escape.
Get out of my VIP section.
Sky Lounge.
Make us.
Super. Remove them.
Barney, I'm a super. Not a bouncer.
It's the same lanyard!
I'm not going anywhere, Barney. I looked up the real building code. Your rope blocks the only exit to the stairwell.
One phone call, and the fire department shuts your VIP section down.
You can't use the building code against the Building Code!
You have your code, Barney. I have mine. Mine has stair widths.
Fine. What do you want?
The truth. Why did you buy this building? And don't say please.
Tax write-off.
Barney.
Sightlines. From the yellow chair, you can see straight into the hot yoga studio across the street.
Oh. Oh, that's why it reclines.
Barney. Tell him. Or I tell him, and I do your voice.
In August, old Mr. Kaplan put the building up for sale. Top bid was a condo developer. Everyone out by spring.
Everyone? Us?
You. Marshall and Lily. Mrs. Fink. The pigeon.
I'd have ended up in Florida.
Ted, my apartment is built so nobody stays past breakfast.
Yours is the only door in New York I've never had to knock on.
You never knock.
Exactly. So I bought the door. And the building around it. For structural reasons.
Then why the rules? The rope, the dress code, the nacho tax?
Ted, I bought a building to save my friends' home. Do you know how lame that is?
I had to be a tyrant. For my image.
And Rule Fourteen? No tenant may ever move out?
That one I meant.
Barney. I'm going to write you a letter.
Oh, no.
With a wax seal.
So the Building Code comes down?
Every rule. Effective immediately.
Wait. All of them? What about the Lily Aldrin Sky Lounge?
The what?
Nothing, baby. Great strike.
Except the nacho tax.
Why that one?
Marshall, I'm sentimental. I'm not crazy. Those nachos are incredible.
Is it me, or did it just get cold? My hip says the boiler's out.
Nobody touch it. That's my boiler.
And she says I have commitment issues.
So it was for the nachos.
Partly, Luke. Uncle Barney collected the nacho tax for six more years. On our couch. Without knocking.
